summary: Northumberland County, PA steel tower reported as planned in 1933, built in 1934, staffed by a named lookout in 1935, and removed before 2006. No source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Register says it was removed before 2006; the removal year is not given

events.note: Newspaper reported an 80-foot tower to be built near Trevorton by CCC workers; one of six towers bought by the U.S. Forest Service as agent
Register gives 1934 as the build year
April 1935 report identifies Isaac Frye as the Trevorton fire tower lookout
April 1935 forest fire on North Mountain, two miles west of Trevorton; three acres destroyed; discovered by the lookout; believed started by a locomotive spark
Upper bound only: register says removed before 2006; the actual year is not given

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The November 1933 newspaper describes a tower still to be built. The register gives 1934 as the build year. The story reports both and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: Brief coordinates (40.762585, -76.718576) and elevation (518 m) match the register. Height 24.4 m is the 1933 report's 80 feet. The brief lists no agency; the 1933 report names the U.S. Forest Service only as purchaser, so agency is left out. Two map and topo listings (Mapcarta, and a Topozone entry seen in search) show a 'Trevorton Fire Tower' point but do not say whether anything stands; they are not used as evidence of status. A Trevorton Heritage Society Facebook post could not be read (login wall). Removal year is not given, so the events entry for 2006 is an upper bound and is labelled that way. Used 2 WebSearch calls and 6 page reads.
